title: Mommy Makeover Compression Garments: How Long to Wear Them
meta_description: Surgeons on the ASPS website say a garment is worn day and night for 1 to 3 weeks, and 4 to 6 weeks after a tummy tuck. What to wear, fit and when to call.
excerpt: Surgeons use compression garments to control swelling after a mommy makeover. Here is how long each piece is worn, part by part and with its source, how a garment should fit, what to wear over it in the heat, and which signs mean you should call your surgeon.
quick_answer:
How long do you wear compression garments after a mommy makeover?

No society publishes one schedule for a whole mommy makeover. Surgeons writing on the ASPS website say a garment is worn day and night for 1 to 3 weeks after plastic surgery in general, and for 4 to 6 weeks after a tummy tuck. The Aesthetic Society says 4 to 6 weeks in a garment over liposuction areas.

images.text_in_image:
How long each garment is worn

No source gives one schedule for a whole mommy makeover.

Compression garment, day and night, except to shower or bathe: 1 to 3 weeks
Compression garment at night, once your surgeon approves: several weeks
Compression garment after a tummy tuck: 4 to 6 weeks
Compression garment over liposuction areas: 4 to 6 weeks
Surgical bra: the first week
Support bra: several weeks after that
Regular bra after a breast lift: about 8 weeks

Your surgeon sets your schedule.

Sources: Daniel Maman, MD, and Cindy Wu, MD, on the ASPS website; The Aesthetic Society; Cleveland Clinic

sources.title: What should I expect during my mommy makeover recovery?
quotes: An elastic bandage or support bra will minimize swelling and support the breasts.
A compression garment may also be used to control swelling in the abdomen, waist and buttocks.

sources.title: Mommy Makeover Cost
quotes: Mommy makeover costs may include:
Post-surgery garments

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Daniel Y. Maman, MD
sources.title: The importance of compression after plastic surgery (2023-09-25)
quotes: Your compression garment should be worn day and night (with the exception of showering or bathing) for anywhere between one to three weeks.
The exact timeframe will vary depending on your body, the procedure you had and any additional factors determined by your plastic surgeon.
After approval from your surgeon, you can expect to wear the garment at night for several weeks.
After your initial follow-up appointment, your surgeon will advise you as to when you can begin removing the compression garment and for how long.
After your procedure, your plastic surgeon should provide you with a fitted compression garment to wear that is approved for medical use at no additional cost.
Maintaining constant pressure on the surgical site will prevent excess build-up of subcutaneous fluid – or swelling – and encourage your body to re-absorb the fluid that accumulates.
Compression garments, however, can help prevent blood cells from moving toward the skin's surface, minimizing the appearance of bruising after surgery.
the pressure applied by a compression garment will help to soften and flatten the area, gradually reducing the appearance of scars.
Your compression garment should fit snugly enough to perform its function but should not be so tight that it is uncomfortable or restricts breathing.
If the garment becomes too loose after the swelling goes down, talk to your plastic surgeon to be fitted for a smaller size.
A compression garment helps to promote circulation and rapid wound healing, which reduces the risk of blood clots and infection.
Note, however, that your compression garment must always be clean to prevent infection at the surgical site.
Because it is important to keep your garment clean to prevent infection, it is fine to periodically remove your garment for cleaning.
However, the goal should be to wear it as consistently as possible to promote the best possible results.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Cindy Wu, MD
sources.title: Answers to common tummy tuck questions (2019-12-17)
quotes: After surgery, you will be placed in a compression garment, which will be worn for 4-6 weeks after surgery to help with reducing swelling.
You will be bent at the waist while standing or lying down for 7-10 days after surgery to protect the incision and to allow for your skin to adapt.
the swelling will continue to diminish until approximately three months post-procedure.

sources.publisher: American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS), quoting Kelly Killeen, MD, and Karen Horton, MD
sources.title: Finding comfort after breast surgery: A guide to compression bras and postsurgical garments (2025-10-30)
quotes: Many patients prefer garments with front closures, making it easy to take on and off without help
No underwire for at least three months,
Most women can return to their normal bras in about one month,
For garments, it's important not to have rough seams against the skin.

sources.title: Mommy makeover: aftercare and recovery
quotes: You will need to wear an abdominal binder after a tummy tuck
You may shower once the dressing, sponges, and gauze pads are removed. This usually occurs within 72 hours.
Wear your compression garment as directed to reduce the likelihood of loose or sagging skin.
Call your surgeon immediately if you notice an increase in swelling, pain, redness, drainage, or bleeding in the surgical area or if you develop fever, dizziness, nausea, or vomiting.
Other red flags include shortness of breath, chest pains, and unusual heartbeat.
Your surgeon may suggest you sleep with several pillows under your back and keep your legs slightly bent at the hips.
You will likely go for a follow-up evaluation with your surgeon within five days.

sources.title: Liposuction: aftercare and recovery
quotes: You will wear a compression garment over the treated areas for four to six weeks to control swelling and promote skin contraction.
You should wait a minimum of six weeks before exposure to sun and heat, including sunbathing, because of the possibility of swelling.
Some surgeons provide these garments, but others will tell you where to purchase them before your surgery.

sources.title: Breast Lift, Cosmetic and Plastic Surgery department
quotes: You’ll need to wear a surgical bra for the first week after surgery, followed by a support bra for several weeks after that.

sources.title: Breast Lift (Mastopexy)
quotes: Usually, women can wear a regular bra about eight weeks after surgery.

sources.publisher: Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Global Open (PubMed abstract; full text via Europe PMC PMC10519563)
sources.title: The Use of Postoperative Compression Garments in Plastic Surgery-Necessary or Not? A Practical Review (Ormseth BH and colleagues, 2023;11(9):e5293)
quotes: The most well-supported indications for the use of postoperative compression garments are to mitigate edema and ecchymosis after rhinoplasty and to reduce postoperative pain after breast and abdominal procedures, although no effect on seroma rate was demonstrated.
patients may be more susceptible to the established consequences of ill-fitting garments, such as discomfort, 23 skin defects and necrosis, 48 and increased venous stasis.
Any potential benefit must be balanced against the associated costs and possible complications of compression, including patient discomfort, increased venous stasis, and skin defects.

sources.title: Effect of Compression Garments on Post-Abdominoplasty Outcomes: A systematic Review of the current Evidence (Arkoubi AY, 2024;41:128-137)
quotes: Only 5 trials totaling 130 patients were included in this review.
Weak evidence supports the beneficial use of abdominal binders following abdominoplasty.

sources.title: Do Compression Garments Prevent Subcutaneous Edema After Abdominoplasty?
quotes: Thirty-two women aged 19 to 50 years were selected and randomly allocated to either the garment (n = 16) or no-garment (n = 16) group.
All patients underwent abdominoplasty and received 10 sessions of manual lymphatic drainage during the postoperative period.
Patients who did not wear a compression garment after abdominoplasty showed less subcutaneous edema formation after 24 days of surgery than those who wore the garment.

sources.title: Everything You Need To Know About Compression Socks
quotes: Your compression socks should provide a decent squeeze, but take them off if they feel uncomfortably tight.
These are all reasons to call your provider.

sources.title: Surgical wound care - closed
quotes: Contact your surgeon if there are any of the following changes around the incision: More redness or pain Swelling or bleeding
You should also contact your surgeon if the drainage coming from or around the incision increases or becomes thick, tan, green, or yellow, or smells bad (pus).
Also contact your surgeon if your temperature is above 100°F (37.7°C) for more than 4 hours.

sources.title: Deep venous thrombosis
quotes: The clot can block blood flow and cause: Redness of the skin Skin that feels warm to the touch Swelling (edema) of a leg or arm Pain or tenderness in a leg or arm
Go to the emergency room or call the local emergency number (such as 911) if you have DVT and you develop: Chest pain Coughing up blood Difficulty breathing Fainting
